notes: LAMOST-HVS1 is classified as follow_up because Table 1 attributes it to Zheng et al. (2014) (T:p2-b0) and §3.1 states it was first discovered by Z14 (T:p4-b1); this paper re-observes/reanalyzes it and retains it among the three HVSs selected by the escape-velocity criterion (T:p3-b7). LAMOST-HVS2 and LAMOST-HVS3 are the two new unbound HVSs announced in the abstract (T:p1-b4) and are therefore candidates_found. Other HVSs appearing only in the literature comparison/Figure 2 (I:p3-b6; T:p3-b6) are not included because this paper does not select or analyze them as target stars.

LAMOST-HVS1: At T:p2-b0/I:p2-b0 the position is printed as (α, δ) = (138°027199, 9°272725); I read these as decimal degrees, consistent with the J2000 coordinate notation. The paper reports both v_los and v_rf for LAMOST-HVS1 at T:p2-b0 and T:p4-b1; only the heliocentric v_los is entered as radial_velocity because v_rf is a Galactic-rest-frame radial component, not a heliocentric/barycentric radial velocity or a total Galactic-rest-frame speed. No parallax, proper-motion values, or bound/unbound probabilities are reported.

LAMOST-HVS2: The equatorial coordinate notation in the table (245°086520, 37°794456) is interpreted as decimal degrees 245.086520 and 37.794456, consistent with the paper's six-decimal coordinate notation (T:p2-b0; I:p2-b0). The paper also reports a Galactic rest-frame radial velocity v_rf = 502.33 ± 8.37 km/s for LAMOST-HVS2 (T:p2-b0; T:p4-b2), but this is a radial component in the Galactic rest frame rather than a heliocentric/barycentric radial velocity, and it is not the total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed; it is therefore not entered under radial_velocity or galactic_rest_frame_velocity. No parallax, proper-motion, bound-probability, or total Galactic rest-frame speed measurements are reported for LAMOST-HVS2.

LAMOST-HVS3: Target: LAMOST-HVS3. The Table 1 position strings are transcribed as (α, δ) = (50°321157, 19°126719) at T:p2-b0 and I:p2-b0; I record them as decimal degrees, RA = 50.321157 deg and Dec = 19.126719 deg, following standard coordinate notation. No parallax, proper-motion components, bound/unbound probability, or total Galactic-rest-frame 3D speed is reported. The tabulated v_rf is a Galactic-rest-frame radial velocity (not a heliocentric/barycentric radial velocity and not a total 3D speed), so it is not included as either radial_velocity or galactic_rest_frame_velocity.
